solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mad, sad and moody in World's End

indicators.note: something mad is crazed and out of order, so the letters that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and sulks in a pub or place called World's End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like the first item in a list of moods, but it is the anagram signal for SAD and MOODY.
explanation.definitionFit: The day of the Last Judgement is the end of the world in Christian belief.

clue.text: Flower in Germany choking slender shrub

indicators.note: to choke something is to grip it round the throat, so one piece closes around the other

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is a river, something that flows; the Oder runs along Germany's eastern border
slender means lean

explanation.surface: A German flower is strangling a thin bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as 'thing that flows', a river: here the Oder.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a poisonous evergreen Mediterranean bush with pink or white blooms.

clue.text: Change bowler is highly successful performer

parts.note: change is loose coins, money
a spinner is a cricket bowler who makes the ball turn

explanation.surface: A cricket captain's change of bowler turns out to be a match-winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change bowler' is a cricket term (a bowler brought on to relieve the opening pair), but here the words split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that earns a great deal of cash is said to be a hugely profitable earner or hit.

clue.text: Shame of French importing rotten cigars

indicators.note: importing means bringing goods in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: rotten things fall apart, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is a scandal that the French are bringing in bad cigars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' reads like a description of the cigars, but it is the anagram signal; 'importing' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonour and loss of respect are what both words describe; a synonym pair.

clue.text: New queen after twelve months or longer

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the period of time

parts.note: twelve months make a year
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A new queen reigns after a year or more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longer' looks like a comparative of long but is the noun: one who longs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who longs for something is one who yearns, so the agent noun fits.

clue.text: Department advocating matricide?

definitions.meaning: a department is a field or sphere of activity
split as ..., an urging to kill one's mother

explanation.surface: A government department seems to be calling for the killing of mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as 'do Ma in', slang for murder Mother; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of responsibility or area of control is a sphere such as a department.

clue.text: Content of metal container is ancient tongue

indicators.note: the content is what is inside, so the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: a tin can is a metal container

explanation.surface: What is inside a metal can turns out to be an old language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content of' takes TIN CAN without its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peruvian empire's language, Quechua, is often called by the people's name; an ancient language of the Andes.

clue.text: Perfume and bible wrapped by mortgagee

indicators.note: something wrapped by another is enclosed in it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a mortgagee is the party who lends money on a mortgage, a lender
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A bank's mortgage pack comes with scent and a Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible is conventionally abbreviated in crosswords; 'wrapped by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The purple-flowered plant gives a fragrant oil used as a scent.

clue.text: In time, soon over obsessive self-love

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the assembled letters are read backwards
In says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an age is a period of time
in a mo, short for in a moment, means soon

explanation.surface: Someone will soon get over a phase of excessive vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts IN A MO inside AGE to give AINAMOGE, and 'over' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An excessive preoccupation with oneself is a mania for the self, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Dracula might attack this French wine, after swallowing tablet

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: vin is French for wine
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Dracula might go for French wine after taking a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: E, for an ecstasy pill, goes inside VIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire bites the blood vessel in the neck, the one he would go for.

clue.text: Run round barrier pursuing terribly aged author

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes after the scrambled one
terribly suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged
round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to race is to run
a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: An old runner goes around a barrier chasing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes EDGA, and 'pursuing' puts the enclosed run after it; 'round' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Wallace was a prolific English thriller writer, co-creator of King Kong.

clue.text: Unpaid work one shouldn't hate doing?

definitions.text: Unpaid work one shouldn't hate doing?

parts.words: Unpaid work one shouldn't hate doing?
parts.note: the phrase for a task done for pleasure rather than money, read playfully as work one ought to enjoy

explanation.surface: Volunteer work is something nobody should resent doing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'shouldn't hate' is a playful gloss on the love in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a task undertaken for enjoyment or devotion rather than reward.

clue.text: Died having suffered flaying back in seaport

indicators.note: back means read in the reverse direction
flaying strips off the skin, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: passed on is a euphemism for died

explanation.surface: Someone died after being skinned alive at a seaport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having suffered flaying' leaves ASSEDO from PASSED ON, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ukrainian city on the Black Sea is a major port.

clue.text: Housemaid reflected light that's elevated

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bonne is French for a housemaid
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a light

explanation.surface: A maid looks at a light in a mirror and feels uplifted.
explanation.walkthrough: BONNE is a French maid; 'reflected' turns it to ENNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised to the peerage, given a noble title, is being raised in rank.

clue.text: Commended as pressure increased

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
raised means increased

explanation.surface: A worker was complimented as the pressure on them grew.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak well of someone is to commend them; a synonym.

clue.text: Water found in some pesticide

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: part means some, a portion
aqua is Latin for water

explanation.surface: Water turns out to contain some weedkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals that the Latin word for water sits inside the word for some.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a highly toxic herbicide, a chemical for killing weeds.

clue.text: Fish unlikely to be sole?

definitions.meaning: a large sea bass of warm waters
one who forms groups would hardly be alone, playing on sole the flatfish

explanation.surface: A fish that is probably not a sole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the flatfish but means solitary.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a heavy-bodied warm-sea fish of the bass family.

clue.text: European or Asian controlled borders?

indicators.note: borders means lies on both sides of, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to run a company is to control it, so ran
an Omani is a person from Oman in Asia

explanation.surface: A European or an Asian was in charge of the frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' is a verb: RAN surrounds OMANI.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Romania is an Eastern European.

clue.text: Letters in stone found in English buildings

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a pile is a large grand building
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Letters carved in stone are discovered in English buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, written st.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal letters, such as those of the New Testament apostles, are known by this word.

clue.text: Make firm series of points to clinch argument

indicators.note: to clinch is to grip tightly, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: S, E and N are compass points in a row
a tiff is a minor argument

explanation.surface: A debater lines up points to win an argument decisively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'series of points' gives compass points S, E, N, which grip TIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To make rigid or harden something is a synonym for firming it up.

clue.text: Nothing 7 keeps in desert is waterproof

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to rat is to desert

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: 7 refers to the answer at 7 down, the ancient tongue
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A desert explorer keeps nothing but a waterproof.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the answer at 7 down; 'keeps' puts O inside it to give INCOA, and 'in' puts that inside the desert word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat worn against the wet is an outer garment made to keep out water.

clue.text: As some streets, old and modern, indeed

parts.note: new means modern
ay is an old form of yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Some streets are both old and modern, indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets that let traffic travel in a single direction are described with this term; an adjective.

clue.text: Sigh, cryptically, what's the matter with such a viewer?

definitions.text: Sigh, cryptically, what's the matter with such a viewer?

parts.words: Sigh, cryptically, what's the matter with such a viewer?
parts.note: the word sigh is sight with its end cut short, so it suggests short sight, the condition of a viewer who cannot see far

explanation.surface: A puzzled sigh: what is wrong with this onlooker?
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sigh' as a shortened 'sight': short sight is the viewer's trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sightedness, the inability to see distant things clearly, is the matter here.

clue.text: Settled on region for sporting fixture

indicators.note: on means placed after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: a quarter is a region or district of a town
final means settled, decided

explanation.surface: A fixture is decided upon for a particular region.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'Settled' first, but 'on' means placed after, so region comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the knockout round of eight teams in a tournament, a match on the calendar.

clue.text: Tailless amphibian beneath a large bush?

indicators.note: beneath in a down clue puts this piece below the first
tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a frog is an amphibian

explanation.surface: A frog with no tail sits under a big shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bush' looks like a shrub but means a thick head of hair; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded, full hairstyle of tightly curled hair resembles a big bush.

clue.text: Single possible locality evacuated

parts.note: on means possible or feasible, as in 'that's not on'

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so just the outer letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: A single possible place has been cleared of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties LOCALITY to LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole, one and no more, is a synonym for single as in 'an only child'.

clue.text: Barker requires excellent wine and beer

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with 1 read as I
red is wine
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A man named Barker demands top wine and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' looks like a surname but is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog barks, and this large terrier from Yorkshire is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Speech from fool in production of Lear

definitions.meaning: the foolish talk or drivel of a fool
Edward Lear wrote comic verse of this kind, such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat

explanation.surface: A speech by the Fool in a staging of King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's King Lear, whose Fool speaks, but it is Edward Lear the comic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd or meaningless talk is drivel; Lear's verse is called this kind of verse.
